title: Canonical Authorization Transaction Commitment
description: §4.3. 'The informal notion of a checkout hash is replaced by a canonical commitment over a normative schema: seller identity, line items with SKU and variant identifiers, quantities, unit and total amounts, currency, tax, shipping, fulfillment source, recurrence terms, and post-authorization substitution policy.' This object is the pre-image; its hash under the binding profile's serialization is the `checkout_commitment` carried by a MandatePatch (§4.2) and the sole input to §3 scoring and the sole permissible display source for §6 challenges. PROFILE-DEFINED: 'each binding profile MUST define the deterministic serialization and hash encoding that make the commitment byte-identical across parties' (§4.3) — this repository ships one such profile, `mandatepatch/profile/v1`, as a choice and not as a normative requirement.

profile.description: §4.3. Identifier of the binding profile whose deterministic serialization and hash encoding produce the commitment. PROFILE-DEFINED: the paper deliberately fixes no serialization; `mandatepatch/profile/v1` is this repository's default.

checkout_id.description: §6.2. Per-checkout distinguisher; 'the patch sequence number and a per-checkout distinguisher displayed' in the challenge rendering.
checkout_id.$comment: PROFILE-DEFINED: identifier syntax and issuing party.

created_at.description: §4.3. Time the candidate commitment was fixed. Each candidate 'is immutable as presented' (§6.1); a changed cart 'is a new canonical commitment requiring fresh evaluation from the beginning' (§4.2).
created_at.$comment: PROFILE-DEFINED: timestamp precision and timezone form. Profile v1 requires RFC 3339 with 'Z' and second precision.

seller_id.description: §4.3. Stable identifier of the seller of record.

legal_name.description: §4.3. Seller's legal name as presented at checkout; also a §3 scoring input and a §6 display field.

merchant_category_code.description: §4.3. Merchant category, where the rail supplies one; explicit null when not applicable.

domain.description: §4.3. Seller's commerce domain; explicit null when not applicable.

currency_minor_unit_exponent.description: Decimal exponent relating minor units to the major unit (2 for USD/EUR, 0 for JPY). PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 carries all monetary values as integer minor units and carries this exponent explicitly so that parties never re-derive it from a currency table that may differ between them.

line_items.description: §4.3, 'line items with SKU and variant identifiers, quantities, unit and total amounts'. §3.1: 'Scoring is performed per line item with worst-case aggregation alongside any cart-level score; authorization never rests on a single cart-centroid embedding, which would permit an out-of-scope item to hide inside an in-scope basket.' PROFILE-DEFINED: array ordering. Profile v1 sorts line items ascending by (sku, variant_id, line_id) compared as UTF-16 code-unit sequences, so producer array order cannot change the commitment.

line_id.description: §4.2. Line-item identifier. For a semantic violation, 'the tuple's value_new encodes the set of approved line-item identifiers within the canonical commitment' — these are those identifiers.

variant_id.description: §4.3, 'and variant identifiers'. Explicit null when the item has no variant axis. The worked example's twelve-pack versus twenty-four-pack distinction lives here or in `title` (§1).

title.description: §4.3. Human-readable item description. Descriptive under Verifiable Intent's split, but load-bearing here: it is a §3 scoring input and a §6 display field, since E₁ 'MUST [be computed] over the canonical authorization transaction commitment defined in Section 4.3 ... never over agent-relayed prose' (§3.1).

unit_amount_minor.description: §4.3, 'unit ... amounts', in integer minor units of `currency`. PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 forbids non-integer numbers anywhere in the commitment.

total_amount_minor.description: §4.3, 'and total amounts', in integer minor units. Carried explicitly rather than derived, so that a producer's rounding cannot silently change the commitment.
§4.3. Total tax in integer minor units.

inclusive.description: §4.3. Whether tax is already included in line totals.

components.description: §4.3. Tax components. PROFILE-DEFINED: array ordering. Profile v1 treats every array other than `line_items` as order-significant and preserves producer order; producers therefore MUST emit components in a stable order.

rate_basis_points.description: §4.3. Rate in integer basis points. PROFILE-DEFINED: rates are integers, not decimals, because profile v1 admits no non-integer numbers.

amount_minor.description: §4.3. Component amount in integer minor units.
§4.3. Shipping charge in integer minor units.

method.description: §4.3. Named shipping or pickup method; explicit null when not applicable.

destination.description: §4.3. Destination. PROFILE-DEFINED: whether the full address or only a commitment to it enters the hash. Profile v1 carries coarse geography in the clear and the precise address as `address_commitment`, so that the commitment can be disclosed to a gateway-side scorer (§3.1) without disclosing the address.

address_commitment.description: Commitment to the full destination address, or explicit null when the address is out of scope for this commitment.

totals.description: §4.3, 'unit and total amounts'. Carried explicitly so that omitted-field drift is 'within the scope of the hash'.

subtotal_minor.description: Sum of line totals, integer minor units.

discount_minor.description: Discounts applied, integer minor units, expressed as a non-negative reduction.

grand_total_minor.description: Amount authorized, integer minor units. This is the value against which a machine-enforceable amount predicate is checked (§2, §4.2).

occurrences.description: §4.3. Bounded occurrence count, or explicit null.

amount_variability.description: §4.3. Whether each charge is fixed or may vary.

max_amount_minor.description: §4.3. Per-charge ceiling for variable recurrence, integer minor units, or explicit null.

recurrence.description: §4.3, 'recurrence terms'. Explicit null for a one-off checkout — never omitted, so that omitted-field drift stays within the scope of the hash.

substitution_policy.description: §4.3, 'post-authorization substitution policy'. §3.2 states the limit plainly: 'goods substituted at fulfillment time — after authorization — are governed only by the committed substitution-policy field as dispute evidence, not blocked live.'

allowed_substitutions.description: §4.3. Enumerated permissible substitutes when `mode` is 'enumerated'; otherwise an empty array (never omitted). PROFILE-DEFINED: array ordering — profile v1 preserves producer order.

variant_id.description: Permitted substitute variant, or explicit null.

max_unit_amount_delta_minor.description: §4.3. Ceiling on unit-price movement a substitution may introduce, integer minor units, or explicit null.

notify_principal.description: §4.3. Whether the principal is notified of a post-authorization substitution. §8 notes that intrinsically noisy markets are better served by 'a coarser mandate with wider category thresholds and an explicit substitution policy, not more patches.'

attempt_nonce.description: §4.3 (v2.3 erratum). Per-attempt distinguisher: a value unique to each checkout attempt (>=128 bits, base64url, no padding). Distinct from checkout_id: platform checkout/session identifiers persist across cart mutations; the attempt nonce does not. Without it, two byte-identical carts produce identical commitments, defeating duplicate detection and §6.1's voiding against re-presentation of a stale attempt.
attempt_nonce.$comment: PROFILE-DEFINED: entropy source. Profile v1 requires 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 chars).

hash_or_null.description: PROFILE-DEFINED hash encoding. Profile v1: SHA-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) serialization, base64url without padding, prefixed with the algorithm name.

marketplace_seller_id.description: Marketplace seller of record, or explicit null.
